verifiedOnChain.operationalNote: cbETH's Pyth price was 2549s old at check time — inside the 3600s maxStaleness bound but not by much. Pyth is a PULL oracle: a low-activity feed stays stale until someone pays to update it. Before a mainnet deploy, push a fresh update for every price id here and re-check, or expect PythSource to withhold and the asset to run on 2-of-3 with no headroom.
verifiedOnChain.chainlinkDescriptionNote: The cbETH feed's on-chain description() is 'CBETH / USD' (capitalised); this file's prose says 'cbETH / USD'. Cosmetic — the address, decimals and answer all verified. The check treats description as advisory and does not fail on wording.

usdcNote: Circle-native USDC on Base (6 decimals). NOT USDbC (0xd9aA...4CA2), the bridged legacy token. Getting this wrong silently prices every vault against the wrong dollar.
maxStalenessNote: One hour, NOT the 'tight (minutes)' figure DEPLOYMENT.md §2 recommends for a pure push-feed stack. That advice is correct for Chainlink and wrong for a stack containing a pull oracle: the Pyth leg only advances when a keeper pays to post, so a 60-second bound drops it from the fresh set on most reads and silently demotes 2-of-3 into 2-of-2 with no failure headroom (asserted in test/MixedOracleSources.t.sol::test_tightStalenessSilentlyDemotesPullLegAndRemovesHeadroom). Tighten this only after measuring the observed worst-case on-chain publish gap for the pinned price ids, or after funding a keeper at a known cadence. Ceiling is 1 day (OracleAggregator.MAX_STALENESS_CEILING).
pythNote: Pyth receiver contract. UNVERIFIED. Pyth deploys the same address across many chains, which makes a copy-paste error from another chain's docs indistinguishable from a correct entry — verify `code.length > 0` on Base specifically, and that getPriceUnsafe returns for each id below.
pythMaxConfBpsNote: Reject a Pyth reading whose confidence interval exceeds 1% of price — a feed in disagreement with itself declines to vote rather than casting an uncertain one. Ceiling is 2000 (PythSource.MAX_CONF_BPS_CEILING).

twapDefaults.cardinalityNote: A V3 pool writes at most ONE observation per block, only on a swap. Base targets 2-second blocks, so covering a 1800-second window in the worst case (a swap every block) needs 1800/2 = 900 slots. `increaseObservationCardinalityNext` is permissionless but the growth is paid per slot (roughly 20k gas each; ~18M gas to go from 1 to 900, so it is done incrementally over several transactions). Check each pool's current `observationCardinality` via slot0() BEFORE deploying: UniswapV3TwapSource's constructor rejects a pool that cannot already serve the window, which is the intended failure — grow the cardinality first, then deploy.
twapDefaults.windowNote: 30 minutes. Bounds are [300, 86400] (MIN_WINDOW/MAX_WINDOW). Longer resists manipulation better and tracks a moving market worse; this is the SF-1 knob, and it is immutable per source.

assets.quorumNote: 2 of 3 — the strict-majority floor for a 3-source set, and the only value that both satisfies OracleAggregator's constructor and leaves one source of failure headroom. Quorum 3 would let any single dark source freeze the asset.

usdcReferenceFeeds.note: NOT wired into any source. Listed because UniswapV3TwapSource pins USDC to $1.00 rather than measuring it, so a sustained depeg mis-prices its leg by exactly the depeg. These two feeds are the off-chain monitoring inputs for that residual (a canary signal, not an on-chain input) — reading USDC/USD on-chain inside the TWAP source would reintroduce the very push-feed dependency the source exists to be independent of.
